title: Tool‑Augmented Post‑Processing of Identical LLM Candidates for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration (shared_initial_candidate evaluation)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1) to isolate whether deterministic post‑processing (a NetOps verifier + lightweight topology simulator) changes a deterministic validator pass/fail outcome when the exact same single LLM candidate is reused verbatim across both pipelines (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Planned: 300 paired tasks (600 episodes). Completed: 598 episodes → 299 complete pairs. Observed contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (both arms accepted identical candidates for all analyzable pairs). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, task manifests, execution log, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 manifests (see Disclosure). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics this run shows no post‑processing effect on the deterministic validator verdict for identical candidates; it does not address independent tool‑augmented generation.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, safe reconfiguration, and configuration repair. A common architectural pattern pairs generation with deterministic validators and simulators to detect or repair unsafe outputs. Empirically attributing improvements to (A) better generation versus (B) deterministic post‑processing requires isolating these components. We preregistered a narrowly scoped, fully archived experiment to ask: when the same single LLM candidate is supplied verbatim to both pipelines, can deterministic verifier+simulator post‑processing change the deterministic‑validator pass/fail verdict? The design, execution, and analysis were automated and archived. The Introduction closes with the research question and contributions. Research question. Does deterministic post‑processing (verifier + simulator) alter the deterministic‑validator pass/fail outcome when both pipelines receive the identical LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics)? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired experiment (cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1) with archived raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, and per‑file SHA‑256s. (2) A reproducible confirmatory analysis reporting the exact observed contingency (n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0) and exact test results. (3) A discussion of ceiling effects, operational implications, and prescriptive guidance for follow‑ups that must vary generation across conditions to evaluate tool‑augmented agents.
sections.related_work: We position this narrow study against recent work on intent→configuration LLMs, RAG/agentic AIOps, and verifier‑augmented generation. Representative verified sources that motivated design choices and the need for reproducible archives include Nguyen et al., 2024 (Intent‑based configuration, doi:10.1002/nem.2313), PreConfig (arXiv:2403.09369), and recent applied agentic AIOps/system papers (e.g., preprints and tool‑augmentation surveys cited in the archive). These sources informed preregistration choices (paired design, difficulty strata, shared_candidate semantics) and the choice to include detailed validator traces and per‑file hashing for auditability. See Cited Record Ids for the exact verified items used for positioning.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 (immutable preregistration SHA‑256: 991674d51794b41cf66471509149237b9a99f709b69aa3408d3d9d2ea2d50fc0). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on a deterministic‑validator pass indicator. Design semantics: shared_initial_candidate — for each task a single LLM generation was produced and reused verbatim by both pipelines. Sample and power. Planned n=300 pairs (150 simple/150 complex). Power target: detect 0.20 absolute paired difference (assumed baseline ≈0.60). Model and orchestration. Declared LLM: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Generation budget: one shared generation per task; maximum provider calls pre‑registered = 600. Deterministic validator and simulator. A domain verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) parses candidate CLI, enforces workflow constraints (e.g., make_before_break, shutdown_configure_restore), computes a final_state in a lightweight topology simulator, emits violation codes, and returns normalized_configuration plus difficulty metadata. The validator's outputs (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, final_state, violation_codes) are archived per episode. Task generation and artifacts. Tasks were synthesized from a deterministic synthetic topology pool with explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, intent text, required_sequence, and difficulty metadata. Each task manifest and its hash are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/execution_manifest.json). Shared_initial semantics and artifact evidence. For each task the single LLM candidate file and the provider call trace are archived. Example authoritative artifacts (representative): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256: 8f38c8be8...), execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json (SHA‑256: fd0462041a...), and the scoring JSONs execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256: 6569b491...) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: cefa6344...). Missingness and failures. The preregistration specified complete‑pair handling: exclude pairs missing both binary outcomes; technical failures logged and archived. One pair (pair‑000269) was excluded due to a provider failure (logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl). All failure traces and logs are archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl; see execution manifest SHA‑256 entries). Archival and hashing. All raw outputs, provider traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces and analysis artifacts were archived and SHA‑256 hashed; the full per‑file manifest is execution/execution_manifest.json (referenced in Disclosure). Analysis. Primary analysis used the frozen executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 with exact McNemar two‑sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed=1729). The analysis inputs and outputs are archived (analysis/*).
sections.results: Execution and sample. Planned: 600 episodes (300 pairs). Completed: 598 episodes; failed: 2; analyzable complete pairs: 299 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Model calls used = 300 (one shared generation per task). Primary confirmatory outcome. The archived 299 complete pairs produce the contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 d77df43abf...): n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Baseline success rate = 299/299 = 100.0%; guarded success rate = 299/299 = 100.0%. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00, 0.00] (artifact: analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c...). Representative per‑task scoring artifacts. Each episode's scoring JSON contains normalized_response, raw_response_sha256, validator_trace with final_state and difficulty metadata. Examples archived: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (sha256 8f38c8be...), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256 6569b491...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256 cefa6344...). Missingness/failures. One pair (pair‑000269) was excluded per preregistered rules due to a provider failure for the shared_initial generation; the provider failure trace and the execution log entry are archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl; refer to execution manifest hashes). The run produced no scorable but discordant pairs in the confirmatory set (zero discordant pairs), producing a degenerate bootstrap CI and a ceiling effect (discussed below). Secondary analyses. No discordant outcomes were observed, so secondary exploratory estimands (simulated outage incidence, cost trade‑offs) are not informative in this shared‑candidate run; raw provider call counts, per‑task latency and model_call counts remain archived for further exploratory inspection (execution/provider_calls/* and execution/responses/*).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. For the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics this run provides an exact, artifact‑traceable factual result: for the 299 analyzable pairs both pipelines accepted the same LLM candidates in every pair (n11=299). This shows that deterministic post‑processing (validator + simulator), when applied after the fact to identical candidates, did not change the binary deterministic validator verdict in this sample. This is an exact observation, not a general claim that validators are unnecessary. Ceiling effect and power. The preregistered power calculation assumed a lower baseline success rate (~0.60) and targeted detecting a 0.20 paired improvement. The observed baseline success = 1.00 produced a ceiling effect that makes the preregistered minimally important effect unobservable in this execution; bootstrap CI degeneracy ([0.00,0.00]) reflects zero observed within‑pair variance. Operational implications. (1) When generation quality is sufficiently high (as in this sample), validators function primarily as auditable confirmations, explicit violation coders, and producible final_state snapshots rather than as decision‑changing repairers in the shared‑candidate setting. (2) Validators and simulators remain essential for audit trails and explicit, reproducible failure explanations (each scoring JSON contains validator_trace with violation codes and final_state). (3) To evaluate whether tool‑augmented agents improve generation outcomes, experimental designs must allow generation to vary between conditions (independent per‑condition generation or agentic tool use during generation), and include adversarial/harder strata to avoid ceiling saturation. Reproducibility. All claims above are reproducible from archived artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json (full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest), execution/responses/*.txt (shared_initial candidates and per‑condition outputs), execution/provider_calls/*.json (provider traces), execution/scoring/*.json (validator traces), analysis/* (paired contingency and analyses). See Disclosure for representative artifact paths and SHA‑256s. Limitations (artifact‑grounded). The experiment isolates only post‑processing for identical candidates (shared_initial_candidate) and cannot assess the effect of tool‑augmented generation. Tasks were synthetic and executed in a lightweight simulator; vendor/device idiosyncrasies and production telemetry are out of scope. A single declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; generalization across models requires replication. The deterministic validator encodes curated workflow invariants but does not exhaustively represent all production behaviors. Recommendations for follow‑ups. (1) Independent per‑condition generation (no shared candidate) to measure generation effects; (2) adversarial/higher‑difficulty tasks to avoid ceiling effects; (3) multi‑model replication and seed variation; (4) instrumented repair‑loop ablations to measure repair iteration contributions (pre‑registered exploratory E1/E2/E3).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study designed to isolate deterministic post‑processing effects given identical LLM candidates. For the 299 analyzable pairs the archived contingency is n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; both arms accepted the identical candidate in every analyzable pair. The observed paired difference is 0.00 (McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This narrow, artifact‑grounded result does not imply validators are unnecessary; rather, it demonstrates that when generation quality is high and identical candidates are evaluated, downstream deterministic validation may confirm rather than change the binary verdict. We archive the complete dataset, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts to enable independent audit and replication, and we recommend follow‑ups that permit per‑condition generation and harder adversarial strata to measure tool‑augmented generation effects.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory; archived pointers and SHA‑256s):
- Initial master prompt (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). This master prompt defined the autonomy boundary and the post‑lock autonomous responsibilities; it is archived and immutable per the track requirement.
- Preregistration: cand_netops_toolagent_003_v1 (preregistration SHA‑256: 991674d51794b41cf66471509149237b9a99f709b69aa3408d3d9d2ea2d50fc0). The preregistration JSON freezes the estimand, sampling plan (300 pairs), shared_initial_candidate semantics, stopping rules, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and missingness rules.
- Declared model and adapter: gpt‑5‑mini (declared in execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). All model and adapter configuration artifacts are archived under execution/*.json and hashed in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Shared_initial_candidate semantics and proof artifacts: for each paired task a single LLM candidate was generated and reused verbatim by both baseline and guarded pipelines. Representative authoritative artifact pointers (all archived and hashed): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256: 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080); execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json (SHA‑256: fd0462041aab1652b92266d9d11d9c3343698b808a6cb9c751a73da573e67950); execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256: 6569b491dbfb2d4b89c947206a71ac05eccf53f2c1e1a45f126b3e229a93f71e); execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: cefa6344888addc12af3f2eab0ec6d6e77d2135fb5481e75dfe3fbf78b0217d5). These artifacts demonstrate that the identical raw candidate (shared_initial) was presented to both pipelines and that both scoring traces accepted it.
- Execution and manifest: the full execution manifest with per‑file SHA‑256 values is archived at execution/execution_manifest.json (see manifest for all file hashes). Key summary values (artifact‑grounded): planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 598; failed episodes = 2; analyzable complete pairs = 299; model_calls_used = 300; maximum_model_calls = 600. The execution log is archived at execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA‑256: b45a600859502b088a9416744ccbff3f5fba2e6dd76b863440bdfd36ebf21bb8).
- Missingness / failure accounting: one pair (pair‑000269) was excluded per the preregistered complete‑pair rule because the shared_initial generation provider call failed. The provider failure trace and execution log record are archived; see execution/provider_calls/task-000269-shared-initial.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl (manifested in execution/execution_manifest.json). The repository contains the provider error record and the execution log entry; the manuscript reports that the failed pair was excluded and that all failure artifacts are archived (no unarchived failures).
- Analysis: primary analysis used the frozen paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 d77df43abf83e081bb5a3c3a21fa0de67afd72628ee5ed880f2bff810e627174; analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c644f8cf7579ff0b2daec77475310d4de96da6a4f1a9266a6ebd72aad). Confirmatory numeric results are reported exactly as archived: complete_pairs = 299; contingency n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap seed = 1729). All analysis inputs and outputs are archived under analysis/ with SHA‑256 values.
- Human involvement and autonomy boundary: The master prompt defines the autonomy boundary. Prior to autonomy lock humans and the Research Director selected the topic family and prepared infrastructure. After the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, generation, execution, deterministic validation, analysis, evidence‑grounded manuscript drafting, AI‑based peer review, and autonomous revision. No manual human editing of the technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; all manuscript quantitative claims map to archived artifacts listed above.
- Reproducibility pointers: the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) contains the authoritative per‑file SHA‑256 map enabling full reproducibility. Representative artifact files and hashes: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json (SHA‑256 fd046204...), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 6569b491...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 d77df43a...). The preregistration and master prompt SHA‑256 values above are the required immutable references.
- Limitations summarized: (1) This study isolates only post‑processing for identical candidates (shared_initial_candidate) and therefore cannot assess whether tool‑augmented generation would improve outputs; (2) tasks were synthetic and executed in a lightweight simulator — external validity to vendor CLIs/firmware and production telemetry is limited; (3) only a single declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; (4) the deterministic validator encodes a curated rule set and cannot exhaustively model all production device behaviors; (5) observed baseline = 100% produced a ceiling effect that made the preregistered minimally important effect unobservable in this execution.
limitations: The confirmatory design used shared_initial_candidate semantics and therefore isolates only downstream post‑processing effects; it cannot assess whether tool‑augmented generation (i.e., allowing the agent to call verifiers/simulators during generation or to produce repaired candidates) would improve generation quality or safety.

Tasks were drawn from a deterministic synthetic topology pool and executed in a lightweight topology simulator; external validity to vendor‑specific CLIs, device firmware idiosyncrasies, or production telemetry is limited.
Only a single declared model family (gpt‑5‑mini) was used; results do not generalize across model families or seeds without replication.

The deterministic validator encodes a curated rule set and workflow invariants (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that are a proxy for operational correctness but cannot exhaustively represent all production hardware behaviors or operator policies.

A ceiling effect occurred (observed baseline success 100%): the preregistered power assumptions were not met and the experiment could not detect the preregistered minimally important paired difference (0.20).
